title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
abstract: arXiv:2611.34247v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI systems increasingly help decide which drug targets enter costly clinical trials. We recast each target-disease hypothesis as a dated event, the pair's first clinical trial. This lets us test whether a language model can forecast such events after its training cutoff, rather than recall events before it. We rebuild a dated biomedical knowledge graph as it stood at the end of each year from 2020 up to its newest version. We then ask six open language models, with and without this graph, which targets will enter a first trial for a disease the next year. Without retrieval, the models rank about as well as trial history, a count of each target's past trials in the same therapeutic area, also after their training cutoffs. Evidence dated before the decision adds at most a small gain, before or after the models' training cutoffs. The newest graph raises five of six models clearly above that baseline, but its paths usually include the answer

translated_title: 模型是预测到了，还是早已知晓？使用时序知识图谱预言机评估大语言模型在新型药物靶点优先级排序中的表现
translated_abstract: AI系统日益参与到决定哪些药物靶点进入昂贵临床试验的决策中。我们将每个靶点-疾病假设重新表述为一个带有日期的事件——即该组合的首次临床试验。这使我们能够测试语言模型是否能在其训练截止日期之后预测此类事件，而不是回忆截止日期之前的事件。我们重建了一个带时间戳的生物医学知识图谱，其内容分别对应2020年至最新版本之间每一年的年末状态。然后我们询问六个开源语言模型——在使用和不使用该图谱的情况下——哪些靶点将在下一年进入针对某种疾病的首次试验。在不使用检索的情况下，这些模型的排名表现与试验历史（即每个靶点在同一治疗领域中过去试验次数的统计）大致相当，即使是在其训练截止日期之后也是如此。无论在模型训练截止日期之前还是之后，决策日期之前的证据最多只能带来微小的提升。最新的知识图谱使六个模型中的五个明显超越了该基线，但其路径中通常已包含了答案。
tldr: 该研究提出一种基于时序知识图谱的评估框架，将药物靶点假设转化为带日期的首次临床试验事件，以区分大语言模型的真正预测能力与记忆，发现无检索的模型仅与简单的历史试验基线相当，而最新知识图谱带来的显著提升可能源于其路径中泄露了答案。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a temporal knowledge-graph oracle framework that recasts drug-target hypotheses as dated first-clinical-trial events to distinguish genuine forecasting from memorization in LLMs, finding that models without retrieval merely match simple trial-history baselines, while the newest graph's clear gains may stem from answer leakage within its paths.
